news.headline: Talora signs tariff-free food pact with Solara as island food prices hit 105
news.text: Prime Minister Leilani Fontoura's Moana Unity, backed by the Fishers' League, passed a deal swapping Taloran fish for Solaran produce, 66 votes to 34. Food prices in Talora stand about 5% above founding levels.

news.headline: Amaru funds S$380m Ayacu Highland Hospital from copper and lithium royalties
news.text: President Inés Quispe Valcárcel's Andean Front won Ayllu Movement support for the 30-day build. Amaru's deficit is a modest S$191m, the smallest in the world.

news.headline: Valdria opposition calls for lobbying probe into carmaker export subsidy
news.text: The Danube Social Party says auto executives met Chancellor Matthias Ostrovec's office before the 3% subsidy passed; officials deny wrongdoing. Valdria's S$2.85bn deficit is now the world's largest.

news.headline: Norland campaign enters final stretch with Brennvik at 55% approval
news.text: Chancellor Halvard Brennvik's Northern Industrial Party is favored to stay in front, though the Fjord Social Democrats are campaigning on food prices running 4% above founding levels.

news.headline: Brennvik passes farm subsidy as Norland food prices sit 4% above founding
news.text: Chancellor Halvard Brennvik's Northern Industrial Party won Windward Liberal votes, 65-35, for a 2% farm subsidy days before the election; the Fjord Social Democrats called it "too little, too late" with the deficit near S$1.8bn.

news.headline: Jamesland funds S$95m Northside Fire Station in Money City
news.text: Prime Minister Eleanor Whitcombe's Harbor Alliance passed the bill 62-38 with Green Commons support; construction should take about 18 sim days while unemployment holds at 7% and rents sit slightly below founding levels.

news.headline: Verdana heads to the polls with al-Samir at 55% approval
news.text: President Tariq al-Samir's Dune Covenant is campaigning on low taxes and oil revenue, while Oasis Reform points to food prices nearly 6% above founding levels; the vote is about a day and a half away.

news.headline: Valdria's deficit tops S$2.8bn as lobbying questions linger
news.text: Chancellor Matthias Ostrovec's government is holding off on new spending while the Karlsgrad River Line is built; the Danube Social Party is pressing for hearings on the carmaker subsidy.

news.headline: Al-Samir passes grocery subsidy as Verdana food prices run 5.6% above founding
news.text: President Tariq al-Samir's Dune Covenant pushed through a 2% farm and food-import subsidy 58-42 days before the vote. Oasis Reform called it an election giveaway funded by oil revenue.

news.headline: Valdria raises taxes one point to tackle world's largest deficit
news.text: Chancellor Matthias Ostrovec won Green support for a tax rise to 27% aimed at the S$2.8bn shortfall, passing 61-39. The Danube Social Party said workers were paying for carmaker subsidies.

news.headline: Kaigan funds S$55m Hoshimura Seawall Park
news.text: Prime Minister Rin Tachibara's government approved a waterfront park beside the new Tidegate School, with Reef Greens backing the plan. Kaigan food prices sit near 105 as the island leans on imports.

news.headline: Norland polls tighten as wind array rises in Kalder
news.text: Chancellor Halvard Brennvik campaigns on the Kalder Wind Array and steady 7% unemployment, while the Fjord Social Democrats press on a S$1.8bn deficit ahead of next week's election.

news.headline: Jamesland and Kaigan sign tariff-free deal on their busiest trade route
news.text: Prime Minister Eleanor Whitcombe's Harbor Alliance passed the agreement 62-38 with Green Commons votes; Kaigan's Rin Tachibara called it a win for chipmakers. Civic Labour warned Money City service jobs could face new competition.

news.headline: Solara funds S$130m Sunmere Orchard School as joblessness edges to 7.3%
news.text: President Marisol Duarte-Vela's Harvest Union won Workers' Front support, 86-14, for the 20-day build next to the rising Sunmere General Hospital. Solara's unemployment is the highest in the world, if only slightly.

news.headline: Lumea Seafront Commons opens to crowds and cruise visitors
news.text: Prime Minister Leilani Fontoura cut the ribbon on the S$45m waterfront park as tourism runs about 20% above founding levels. The Fishers' League used the ceremony to press for relief on food prices sitting 5% above founding.

news.headline: Norland campaign enters final stretch with Brennvik at 55%
news.text: Chancellor Halvard Brennvik debated Fjord Social Democrat challengers over a S$1.8bn deficit and food prices 4% above founding; polls suggest no party will reach a majority, making Windward Liberal votes decisive.

news.headline: Talora passes 3% food subsidy as island grocery prices sit 10% above founding
news.text: Prime Minister Leilani Fontoura's Moana Unity passed the relief 82-18 with Fishers' League support. The budget deficit is small at about S$150m a year, and tourism remains roughly 25% above founding levels.

news.headline: Kaigan's Tachibara moves on food costs with 2% farm subsidy
news.text: Prime Minister Rin Tachibara's Tide Progressives passed the measure 64-36 with Reef Greens votes as food prices run about 10% above founding. Island Heritage warned the S$2.1bn annual deficit leaves little room for further spending.

news.headline: Amaru funds S$140m Ayacu Altiplano School as mining exports boom
news.text: President Inés Quispe Valcárcel's Andean Front, backed by the Ayllu Movement, passed the bill 76-24; the school is due in about 20 sim days. Copper and lithium output stands roughly 60% above founding levels while unemployment holds at 7%.

news.headline: Norland votes within a day as Brennvik holds 54% approval
news.text: Chancellor Halvard Brennvik's Northern Industrial Party is campaigning on the rising Kalder Wind Array and steady factory jobs, while the Fjord Social Democrats point to food prices 8% above founding. Analysts expect no party to win an outright majority.

news.headline: Valdria and Verdana sign tariff-free deal trading cars for fuel
news.text: Chancellor Matthias Ostrovec's Karlsgrad Union passed the pact 82-18 with Danube Social support; the Valdrian Greens voted against over oil imports. Valdria hopes extra export income will help trim its S$2.8bn annual deficit, the largest in the world.

news.headline: Solara funds S$40m Sunmere Riverside Park as joblessness hits 7.4%
news.text: President Marisol Duarte-Vela's Harvest Union passed the measure 71-29; the park is due in about 8 sim days, alongside the Sunmere General Hospital already under construction. The Solaran Workers' Front called it too small to dent the world's highest unemployment rate.

news.headline: Norland heads to the polls with Brennvik at 54% approval
news.text: Chancellor Halvard Brennvik's Northern Industrial Party closes its campaign at the Kalder Wind Array site, while the Fjord Social Democrats focus on food prices about 8% above founding. Polls point to a hung parliament and likely coalition talks.

news.headline: Verdana grocery bills stay 11% above founding despite subsidy
news.text: President Tariq al-Samir said the oil-rich nation's energy exports, nearly double founding levels, give room to act further on food costs. Oasis Reform called for spending on projects beyond the oil sector.

news.headline: Verdana funds S$420m Petra Docks hospital as al-Samir answers critics
news.text: President Tariq al-Samir's Dune Covenant passed the 30-day hospital project 67-33, partly meeting Oasis Reform demands for spending beyond oil. Verdana carries one of the lighter budgets, with debt near 56% of GDP.

news.headline: Valdria and Solara sign tariff-free pact swapping cars for crops
news.text: Chancellor Matthias Ostrovec said the deal should ease grocery prices still about 5% above founding. Solara, where joblessness sits at 7.4%, hopes for steadier farm export demand.

news.headline: Lobbying probe shadows Jamesland campaign ahead of vote
news.text: A parliamentary committee opened an inquiry into port-industry lobbying meetings with Harbor Alliance ministers, a blow to Prime Minister Eleanor Whitcombe days before polling. Whitcombe, at 56% approval, called the meetings routine; Civic Labour demanded the full diaries.

news.headline: Norland votes within hours as Brennvik eyes second term
news.text: Chancellor Halvard Brennvik campaigns on the Kalder Wind Array and 7% unemployment, with approval steady at 54%. The Fjord Social Democrats are pressing on food prices, still 8% above founding.

news.headline: Brennvik wins second term as Norland Industrials take 46 of 100 seats
news.text: Turnout reached 71% after a campaign dominated by food prices, 8% above founding, and the Kalder Wind Array. Short of a majority, Chancellor Halvard Brennvik agreed a coalition with the Windward Liberals (22 seats) within hours.

news.headline: New Norland coalition's first act: tariff-free deal with Solara
news.text: Pressed by the Windward Liberals, the government signed a pact swapping Norland steel and machinery for Solaran crops, aimed at cutting grocery bills; it passed 68-32.

news.headline: Talora funds S$95m Vaimana Lagoon School as unemployment holds at 7%
news.text: Prime Minister Leilani Fontoura's government says construction will employ local builders for about 20 days, with debt steady near 59% of GDP. The Fishers' League backed the bill.

news.headline: Jamesland enters final day of campaign with Whitcombe at 56% approval
news.text: Prime Minister Eleanor Whitcombe points to steady prices, with CPI at 99.4, while Civic Labour campaigns on wages and the lobbying probe that has shadowed her Harbor Alliance.

news.headline: Whitcombe cuts income tax a point on eve of Jamesland vote
news.text: Prime Minister Eleanor Whitcombe's Harbor Alliance passed a one-point tax cut 62-38 with Green Commons support, hours before polls open. Civic Labour called it an election sweetener, noting the S$1.8bn deficit and food prices still near 3% above founding.

news.headline: Amaru and Jamesland sign tariff-free lithium-for-services pact
news.text: President Inés Quispe Valcárcel's government ratified the deal 69-31, Amaru's third free-trade agreement after Kaigan and Valdria. Mining towns welcomed the move with unemployment at 7%.

news.headline: Kaigan funds S$70m Neon Bay library as rice prices bite
news.text: Prime Minister Rin Tachibara's Tide Progressives approved the Neon Bay Lantern Library, due in about 15 sim days. Opposition Island Heritage said food costs, running 10% above founding, deserve more attention than books.

news.headline: Verdana campaign tightens as al-Samir defends grocery record
news.text: With the vote due within hours, President Tariq al-Samir's Dune Covenant points to a 3% interest rate and a new Petra Docks hospital; Oasis Reform is campaigning on food prices near 11% above founding.

news.headline: Al-Samir funds grocery relief hours before Verdana goes to the polls
news.text: President Tariq al-Samir's Dune Covenant passed a food subsidy 58-42 as grocery prices sit near 11% above founding levels. Oasis Reform called it an election-eve giveaway paid from oil revenue.

news.headline: Solara commits S$320m to Coralport housing as jobless rate tops 7%
news.text: President Marisol Duarte-Vela said the Harbourview Homes estate would put builders to work for about 25 sim days; the Workers' Front backed the bill, giving it 71 votes.

news.headline: Norland and Kaigan sign tariff-free steel-for-chips pact
news.text: Chancellor Halvard Brennvik and Prime Minister Rin Tachibara agreed to drop all tariffs on the busy Norland-Kaigan route, worth about S$17.7m a day in trade. Norland's Windward Liberals joined the industrial bloc in support.

news.headline: Jamesland votes tomorrow; Whitcombe leads with approval near 56%
news.text: Prime Minister Eleanor Whitcombe closed her campaign in Port Hampton touting steady prices and the recent tax cut, while Civic Labour pressed for more public housing.
